metadata.name: Mushroom Keychain v3 - Click-Together, Zero Supports
metadata.description: v3 after the v2 design review: (1) spores now show their ROUNDED side (cut face buried in the cap) - real amanita warts are rounded bumps, and v2's flat-face-out pads produced concave waists; (2) the 4 inner spores are smaller than the 8 outer ones; (3) the stem is a SEPARATE part joined by a snap-fit click post - this lets the cap print display-face-UP with every surface fully supported (v2's flipped one-piece print left the 8 slope spores as floating islands over air). Cap: TRUE dome - ellipsoid cut at its equator, widest circle at the base, 5mm tall over o28mm, zero overhang printed face-up with a snap socket (o6.4 bore, internal groove, entry chamfer). Stem: tapered cone with a slotted click post (o6.2 shaft, o6.7 rounded snap ring, 2.4mm flex slot, ~3.5% prong strain - PLA-safe) and the o3mm keyring hole. Exports THREE STLs: red cap + white spores (same origin, import together as one multi-part object) and the white stem (own object, prints standing). No flips, no supports, no bridges.

commands.description: Set scene to millimeters.
Wipe the scene for an idempotent replay.

PHASE 1: cap blank - ellipsoid with z semi-axis 5mm on r14. The equator (widest circle, r14) sits exactly at Z=22 where the bottom cut lands, making the cap a TRUE DOME: widest at its base, wall starting vertical at the plate and curving inward to the apex at Z=27 - no under-curl, no overhang ring (design review: the cap must be a dome, not a flying saucer).
Bottom slice cutter - top face at Z=22, the ellipsoid's EQUATOR: the flat base is the widest cross-section, so printing face-up has zero overhang anywhere on the cap.
Slice the cap at its equator: a 5mm-tall dome, o28 base. This face is the build-plate face AND the mating plane where the cap seats on the stem shoulder.
Snap socket bore cutter - o6.4, reaching 3.4mm into the cap (to Z=25.4, leaving a 1.6mm roof under the apex at 27). Extends below the bottom face so no coplanar-face boolean flakiness.
Cut the socket bore. The stem's o6.2 shaft slides in with 0.1mm/side clearance.

Internal groove cutter - torus reaching r3.5 at Z=24 (2.0mm above the mating plane at 22, same station as the stem's snap ring). The rounded groove profile lets the click disengage if you ever want the parts apart.
Cut the annular snap groove into the bore wall (lip depth 0.15mm over the bore radius).
Entry chamfer cutter - widens the socket mouth from o7.4 to o6.4 over the first 0.9mm. Guides the post in AND cancels first-layer elephant-foot squeeze at the bore opening.
Cut the entry chamfer.
Bake the dome slice and the full snap socket. *** END OF PHASE 1 *** Stop here to view: domed cap with click socket.

PHASE 2: inner-spore template (r2.2 - SMALLER than the outer ring per design review), squashed z-scale 0.4. Built AT THE WORLD ORIGIN so origin == mesh center survives any addon version (some builds bake location at creation; a template elsewhere makes rotated duplicates swing around a phantom pivot).

Template cutter - top face at Z=-0.2: removes the BOTTOM of the lens, keeping the rounded dome up. The cut face gets buried in the cap and the ROUNDED side shows - real amanita warts are rounded bumps, not flat pads (v2's flat-face-out look was the review's main complaint).
Cut the inner template: dome up, flat underside 0.2 below its equator (~61% kept - 'cut at least half' of the squashed sphere).
Bake the template cut BEFORE duplicating (live modifiers on duplicates cut in wrong world positions).
Inner spore East - ring r=5 on the new 5mm dome (surface 26.68), cut face sunk ~0.25, tilted 8 degrees outward to match the local slope.
Inner spore North. - ring r=5 on the new 5mm dome (surface 26.68), cut face sunk ~0.25, tilted 8 degrees outward to match the local slope.
Inner spore West. - ring r=5 on the new 5mm dome (surface 26.68), cut face sunk ~0.25, tilted 8 degrees outward to match the local slope.
Inner spore South - ring r=5 on the new 5mm dome (surface 26.68), cut face sunk ~0.25, tilted 8 degrees outward to match the local slope.
Remove the inner template.
Outer-spore template (r2.6, the bigger ring), squashed z-scale 0.4, again at the world origin.
Template cutter - top face at Z=-0.25: keeps the rounded dome with a flat underside.
Cut the outer template.
Bake before duplicating.
Outer spore 1 of 8 - ring r=9.8 (surface 25.57), cut face sunk ~0.35 (deeper: the dome is curvier here), tilted 19 degrees to match the local slope.
Outer spore 2 of 8 (67.5 degrees). - ring r=9.8 (surface 25.57), cut face sunk ~0.35 (deeper: the dome is curvier here), tilted 19 degrees to match the local slope.
Outer spore 3 of 8 (112.5 degrees). - ring r=9.8 (surface 25.57), cut face sunk ~0.35 (deeper: the dome is curvier here), tilted 19 degrees to match the local slope.
Outer spore 4 of 8 (157.5 degrees). - ring r=9.8 (surface 25.57), cut face sunk ~0.35 (deeper: the dome is curvier here), tilted 19 degrees to match the local slope.
Outer spore 5 of 8 (202.5 degrees). - ring r=9.8 (surface 25.57), cut face sunk ~0.35 (deeper: the dome is curvier here), tilted 19 degrees to match the local slope.
Outer spore 6 of 8 (247.5 degrees). - ring r=9.8 (surface 25.57), cut face sunk ~0.35 (deeper: the dome is curvier here), tilted 19 degrees to match the local slope.
Outer spore 7 of 8 (292.5 degrees). - ring r=9.8 (surface 25.57), cut face sunk ~0.35 (deeper: the dome is curvier here), tilted 19 degrees to match the local slope.
Outer spore 8 of 8 (337.5 degrees). - ring r=9.8 (surface 25.57), cut face sunk ~0.35 (deeper: the dome is curvier here), tilted 19 degrees to match the local slope.
Remove the outer template.
Join all 12 rounded spores into the white cap-decoration body. *** END OF PHASE 2 *** Stop here to view: domed cap with rounded warts.
PHASE 3: stem - SEPARATE PART, built standing at X=30. Tapered cone, base r=5 on the plate, shoulder r=4 at Z=20. The cap's flat underside seats on this shoulder when clicked together.
Click post - o6.2 shaft rising 3.3mm above the shoulder (socket is 3.4 deep: 0.1 bottoming clearance), rooted 0.3mm into the stem tip.

Snap ring - rounded bulge to r3.35 at 2.0mm above the shoulder, the SAME station as the cap's groove. 0.15mm interference against the o6.4 bore; the round profile self-guides on insertion and allows deliberate removal.

UNION the post into the stem - NOT join_objects: joining overlapping closed shells makes a self-intersecting mesh that the EXACT boolean solver later reduces to nothing (we watched the stem export 0 triangles). Union produces one clean manifold shell.
Bake the post union.
UNION the snap ring onto the post.
Bake the ring union - the stem is now a single manifold shell, safe to cut.
Remove the (hidden) union operands so they cannot reach the exports.

Flex slot cutter - 2.4mm slot through the post down into the stem tip (Z 18.4-23.8). Splits post and ring into two 1.9mm prongs; each flexes 0.15mm on insertion = ~3.5% strain, safe for a one-time PLA click (PETG clicks forever). The slot shows as a small 1.6mm notch on the stem sides below the shoulder - hidden once assembled.
Cut the flex slot.
Keyring hole cutter, radius 1.5 (o3mm - reduced 25% from the o4 draft that looked oversized on the stem). Near the stem base with a 3.5mm wall below.
Cut the o4mm keyring hole.
Bake slot + hole. *** END OF PHASE 3 *** Stop here to view: stem with click post and keyring bore.
Remove all cutter objects so nothing stray can reach the exports.

PHASE 4: drop the cap (dome base was modeled at Z=22) so its flat underside sits on Z=0, plate-ready display-face-up. Pure translation via location_offset - origin-independent, immune to the deployed addon's location-baking. One object per call (the bridge schema silently drops lists).
Drop the spores by the same 22mm so they stay socketed on the cap dome - same-origin alignment preserved for the multi-part slicer import.
Red material for the cap (hex base_color - RGBA 'color' lists are an outdated schema).
White material for spores and stem.
Cap goes red.
Spores and stem go white.
Waterproofing check on the red cap body (with socket).
Waterproofing check on the 12 spore shells.
Waterproofing check on the stem with click post.
Export the red cap STL - flat face on Z=0, display-face-up, plate-ready. Same world origin as the spores: import these two together as ONE multi-part object.
Export the white spores STL (same origin as the cap).
Export the white stem STL - its own object, prints standing beside the cap. Import it in a SECOND import action so it does not merge into the cap's multi-part object.
